dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHARDFALL ARENA VAULT

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE MASK
dialogueInline.text: Gate manifests. Independent inspection. Then the cargo moves.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: It's grain. It's been grain since it left the field. You can count it at the destination.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE MASK
dialogueInline.text: If we cannot verify the shipment, the Shards cannot guarantee their share.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: My crew's families are Shards. We haven't seen our share either. You'll have to explain to them why a load meant for Auric can't be allowed through while they're starving on this side.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE MASK
dialogueInline.text: You confuse immediate discomfort with a lasting political advantage.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: My youngest can't tell the difference. She keeps asking what we're having for supper.

panelPlan: SHARDFALL ARENA VAULT. The Trade Mask sits before a captain whose ship has been held in the picket. The captain's crew has medical patients at home and.
Trade's emissary removes the captain's transit permit. The political argument is over; hunger isn't.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC GOVERNOR CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Two openings. The first is narrower, but the timing is stable. The second is thirty minutes later. Nothing about either one guarantees the ships beyond the picket will behave.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Food first. Medicine through the second.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: People will accuse you of sending grain while patients wait.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: They may. The first freighters have enough thermal margin to hold the narrow approach. The medical craft don't. We lose both loads if we make them trade places.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: That is an actual reason. You should give that to the people who will complain.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I intend to.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Publish both times?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Publish verified updates, not the next guess someone sells to a desperate captain.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: You really are enjoying this.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: More than you think.

panelPlan: AURIC GOVERNOR CHAMBER. Two measurable Gate windows are available tonight, thirty minutes apart. Shard pickets physically obstruct both. Halev, Naomi and Jex.
Jex opens the updates. Naomi walks out to Sunlash, leaving Halev with the medical-transport families who have just heard they're second.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THUNDERBREAK COMMAND

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: All the Shard identifiers went silent.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Positions?

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Unchanged. They're still there.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Then nobody fires at an empty patch of space because the name beside it went away. Mark their measured positions. Tell Gravefire where our cover begins and ends.

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: It's unusual to coordinate with a vessel our own reports still call hostile.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: The patients don't benefit from the distinction. Our weapons remain governed by Fleet orders. Our charts need to show what's actually present.

panelPlan: THUNDERBREAK COMMAND. The Shard pickets remain exactly where they were, but their transponders disappear.
Her limited commission does not change who commands Thunderbreak. Deka acknowledges the tactical exchange from her captain's station.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: ARENA VAULT

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE MASK
dialogueInline.text: No manifest, no crossing.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: The doctors have listed the patients. You want names of the people escorting them and every household they're carrying medicine to. You don't need that to know whether the hold contains antibiotics.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID MASK
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire will enforce the medical blockade.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID MASK
dialogueInline.text: Relinquish your Gate-line posting.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I'll surrender the posting. I'm taking Gravefire with me.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID MASK
dialogueInline.text: Your ship is not exempt from Confederacy obligations.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Neither is my crew exempt from the obligations I have to them. They follow my command aboard Gravefire. You can appoint another Gate-line captain. You can't make this one pretend the patients aren't ours.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You could have warned me before you did that.

panelPlan: ARENA VAULT. Abby stands beside Tess when Trade insists on inspection control over the second medical convoy. The drugs are destined partly for Shard patients..
The word lands without theatrics. Abby looks at her sister, who doesn't look back.
Outside the chamber Abby catches Tess.
directionInline: Use released Rex Fleet references for appearance, faction and ship design. Preserve exact dialogue, action and speaker order.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I thought the look on my face was plenty of warning.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: We need seven captains to hold their position for half an hour. They can lose their berths if they do it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You can't make the decision for them.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I know.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Then ask. And let them say no without calling them cowards. I'll take the medical skiffs. You're better at making people listen. I was never any good at it.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You just told the Triarch no to their faces.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: They were listening. I wouldn't call it a friendly conversation.

panelPlan: Abby reaches to straighten a damaged cuff on Tess's flight suit. Tess pulls away, then lets her finish.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SUNLASH HANGAR AND AURIC GATE

dialogueInline.speaker: PILOT
dialogueInline.text: Could we wait for the second opening? It looks wider.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: That one belongs to the medics. We're taking the one we can safely reach.

dialogueInline.speaker: PILOT
dialogueInline.text: Safely?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: More safely than trying to steal somebody else's thirty minutes.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND
dialogueInline.text: Freighter Two took the marker. Mast's damaged.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Keep them on course. They can replace a mast after docking. They can't replace the ship if they panic and chase the marker back into the field.

panelPlan: SUNLASH HANGAR AND AURIC GATE. Naomi chooses the exposed lead route to keep two food freighters clear of the worst shear. The windows are physical, measured.
She leads. One freighter clips an anchor marker in slow approach; its mast buckles without destroying the ship.
The food ships arrive. At Auric, the damaged mast delays unloading. Halev moves the crews to the undamaged ship first instead of pretending all freight is.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHARDFALL — CAPTAIN COMMUNICATIONS

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I'm asking you to rotate your weapons away from the medical lane. I am not asking for your ships. Keep your crews. Keep your stations. When the window closes, you'll answer to your own people for what you did.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN ONE
dialogueInline.text: Raid will freeze my berth.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Probably.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN TWO
dialogueInline.text: You can't give me another.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN THREE
dialogueInline.text: If we're fired on, do you guarantee we'll survive?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I can guarantee you'll know where the medics are. Anything beyond that would be a lie.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: No. Leave them requests. If I need obedience to make this work, it's already the wrong kind of victory.

panelPlan: From Shardfall, Trade learns its loyalist replacement force cannot arrive before the second window. Abby reaches seven captains with a message each can refuse.
She hears the long silences after sending the instructions. Some captains answer cautiously. Others say nothing until the deadline. Her officer offers to send.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC GATE — SECOND WINDOW

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: You don't have enough reserves for another engagement.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I'm not planning to make one. They're going through.

dialogueInline.speaker: LOYALIST CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Ashfang, get out of the line.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You can see who's behind me. You fire, everybody sees which side of my ship you wanted to hit.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Sunlash, the inner mouth is open. Medical One is clear. Medical Two, keep your nose where I can see it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Fleet secured both windows.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Fleet secured its own lane. Those seven captains decided not to fire. Our report needs to say that.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: And Ashfang kept the loyalist from taking the shot.

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: She's the one who destroyed our relief crates last crossing.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I know. I don't intend to send her a thank-you bouquet. Put the actual maneuver in the log.

panelPlan: Gate's second opening. Seven independent captains each rotate their guns away at their own times. A loyalist patrol moves to stop the medical convoy. Billie.
The loyalist holds fire. Tess guides the skiffs with Gravefire; cooling levels continue to constrain her maneuvers.
The convoy passes. On Thunderbreak, a junior officer celebrates Fleet's accomplishment.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: TAL CORVUS SERVICE WARRENS

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: It wasn't here yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Yesterday we were busy trying to persuade the same people not to shoot us. Take a sample before it disappears.

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: You think it's dangerous?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I don't know what it is. I'm not going to improve it by naming it a curse.

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: We have found the people who make the information move. Now learn why the others trust them.

panelPlan: TAL CORVUS SERVICE WARRENS. Tess walks the reopened flow path with a technician. A physical seep along the structural seam behaves differently from normal.
Elsewhere Fear's emissary presents a network of named civilian couriers who spread actual route updates.
The unknown seep remains measured but unexplained. The political campaign against witnesses is considerably easier to understand.
